objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a breast mass.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I found a mass in my right breast about three weeks ago, and it’s grown very quickly. I haven’t had any pain, and I haven’t noticed any skin or nipple changes.
Doctor: May I ask how old you are?
Patient: I’m 45 years old.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in the size of the mass since you first felt it, and if so, how quickly has it grown?
Patient: It’s grown noticeably since I first felt it about three weeks ago—it seemed to enlarge very rapidly over that time. I’d say the size increase has been significant within those weeks.
Doctor: Do you feel any tenderness
Patient: No, I don’t feel any tenderness or pain when I notice or touch the mass.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes to the skin over the lump—such as dimpling, redness, or thickening—or any changes to the nipple, like discharge or inversion?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any skin dimpling, redness, or thickening, and there hasn’t been any nipple discharge or inversion. I also haven’t felt any swollen lymph nodes that I can tell.
Doctor: Where on the right breast is the lump located (e.g., upper outer quadrant, central, near the nipple), and does it feel mobile or fixed when you press on it?
Patient: It feels like it’s in the right breast, but I’m not sure exactly which quadrant—it seems more in the outer area. When I press on it, it feels fairly firm and doesn’t seem very mobile.
Doctor: Does the size or tenderness of the lump change at any point in your menstrual cycle, such as becoming larger or more tender just before your period?

Patient: I haven’t noticed any clear connection to my menstrual cycle—no particular increase in size or tenderness around my period. The mass has just been steadily and rapidly growing over the past three weeks.
Doctor: Have you had any recent changes in your overall health, such as unexplained weight loss, fever, night sweats, or fatigue?

Patient: I haven’t had any unexplained weight loss, fever, night sweats, or any changes in my appetite, and I don’t feel unusually fatigued. Overall, I feel the same aside from the rapidly growing mass in my right breast.
Doctor: Do you have any personal or family history of breast cancer or other cancers (especially first‑degree relatives such as mother, sister, or daughter)?
Patient: I don’t have any personal history of breast masses or cancer, and there’s no family history of breast cancer or other cancers in first-degree relatives.
Doctor: Are you currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or have you been using hormonal contraceptives or hormone‑replacement therapy recently?
Patient: No, I’m not pregnant or breastfeeding, and I haven’t been using hormonal contraceptives or hormone-replacement therapy recently.
